config.text: A shot is a %%0%%: wide gives context, close gives feeling, an insert gives information. A cut is %%1%%: what follows changes what the previous shot meant. And montage builds %%2%% that no single image contains — the unit of cinematic meaning is the relationship between images.
config.hint: Film is a language learned, not born into — and like language it has grammar.

activities.caption: file each fact by its context

config.prompt: Films do not fall from the sky — file each fact by its context:

items.label: Battleship Potemkin commissioned for the revolution's twentieth anniversary
Citizen Kane as a cipher of William Randolph Hearst
New Hollywood as post-Vietnam cynicism on screen
the studio system's contract players and house styles
streaming platforms' release windows and algorithmic dashboards
the audits of whose stories get financed

config.why: Reading a film in context means holding all of these at once: the shot, the grammar, the movement it belongs to, and the world that paid for it.

activities.anchor: Two people talk at a table and a bomb goes off
activities.caption: same scene, two cuts — drag between them
activities.name: gocBombCompare

config.prompt: One table, one bomb, two versions — drag the divider:

before.label: the surprise cut
before.text: The blast lands unannounced: fifteen seconds of shock, and then the scene is over.

after.label: the suspense cut
after.text: The audience is shown the bomb first — plain, ticking, while the small talk continues. Minutes of engagement: every innocent line about the weather tightens the screw.

config.why: Information management — what the audience knows, when, relative to the characters — is the director's master lever.

activities.anchor: a sudden shock beats sustained suspense
activities.caption: true or false — the bomb-theory audit
activities.name: gocBombJudge

statements.s: An unexpected explosion buys minutes of engagement.
statements.why: It buys seconds of surprise — the audience shown the bomb first spends minutes gripping every innocent line.

statements.s: Information the audience holds is the tension; the bang merely spends it.
statements.why: That is the bomb theory's whole argument about information management.

statements.s: Suspense requires the characters to know about the bomb too.
statements.why: The engine is the gap: the audience knows something the characters do not.

statements.s: A withheld insert or a cutaway to the detonator redistributes knowledge between viewer and characters.
statements.why: A point-of-view shot, a withheld insert, a cutaway — each is pure grammar doing information management.
